Chapter 10: The Power of Story—Changing the Narrative, Changing the World
Have you ever noticed how stories help us make sense of everything around us? They shape what we believe, the values we hold close, and even what we imagine is possible.
Think about Ali’s story for a second. For years, it was overlooked—almost forgotten. But now, just by telling it, we can change the way people see science, history, and maybe even themselves.
There’s a moment, late in the book, where a young writer sits down, ready to share Ali’s life. You can almost feel the tension—wondering, “What if I don’t get this right? What if I can’t do Ali justice?” But there’s hope, too. Because by speaking Ali’s name, by bringing this story into the light, they’re reshaping how we remember the past.
And here’s something we often forget: you have the power to change the story, too. Every time someone remembers a life that’s been ignored, or lets a new voice be heard, the world gets a little more honest. A little more just. Ali’s story isn’t just about what happened long ago—it’s about what’s next. It’s about the kind of world we want to create together.
So, as the book comes to a close, what sticks with you is possibility. Sure, the work of remembering and recovering these stories is never really done. But each time we choose to tell a fuller, truer story, we move one step closer to justice.
Ali’s story? It’s a call to action. It’s a reminder that we all have a part to play if we want a world that’s more fair, more inclusive, and, above all, more true.
